name: Sadiq Khan
role: Mayor of London (2016-); Labour MP for Tooting (2005-2016); Shadow Justice Secretary (2010-2015)
summary: Labour politician of the soft left who has led London's government since 2016. His record and words stress affordable and council housing, public services, climate and air-quality action, tough-and-preventive policing, openness to migrants and diversity, human rights and civil liberties in the Commons, and closer ties with Europe after Brexit.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Pledges to be a champion for the NHS and to push for improvements through the London Health Board; backs the publicly provided service.

public-ownership.rationale: No recorded position on public ownership of major industries.

unions-good.rationale: Says he has stood up for workers' rights and worked with trade unions, and backs a New Deal for Working People and renters' unions.

worker-ownership.rationale: Backs the London Ownership Hub to realise the benefits of democratic and cooperative business, a voluntary route rather than a general rule.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Wants a public-health approach to drugs but robust enforcement against dealers and 'tough enforcement' as drugs drive crime; legalisation is not part of it.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Defended the Racial and Religious Hatred Bill in the Commons, rebutting the objection that it was a sop to Muslims.

decide-locally.rationale: Says Labour embraces devolution and would devolve skills, transport and economic development; seeks further devolution of rail powers to London.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: LabourList's whip-by-whip table lists him among Labour MPs who voted for the Marriage (Same Sex Couples) Bill at second reading in February 2013.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Calls the climate crisis one of the biggest threats we face and sets a net-zero London by 2030, faster than any comparable city.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: As Mayor he hosted a City Hall event celebrating the coronation of King Charles III.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: As a minister told the Commons that sharia law has no jurisdiction in England and Wales and there is no intention to change that; religious councils must comply with equality law.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Said those alleged to have committed or been complicit in torture for the UK should be properly investigated, prosecuted and punished.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: In his manifesto he says London's diversity 'is not a weakness, but our greatest strength'.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Campaigned for Remain and wants the UK in the single market and customs union and supports EU cooperation on justice and policing.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Commits to build council homes for rent and capped-rent homes for key workers, so he cannot hold that renting out housing should be prohibited.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Attacked the government's limits on judicial review and legal aid as taking away citizens' power to challenge power.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Spoke in the Commons of the dehumanisation and hatred that led to the killing of 6 million people and paid tribute to survivors.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Told CNN that Islam and the West are not incompatible: it is possible to be a Muslim and live in the West, and saying otherwise plays into the extremists' hands.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Pledges to bear down on both antisemitism and Islamophobia and to defend openness, equality and inclusion for all faith communities.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Has doubled City Hall's police funding, pledges 1,300 more officers and says he will always support the police to bear down on criminals.

rent-control.rationale: No recorded position on a general legal cap on rents; his Rent Control Homes are a limited scheme for key workers.

second-chamber.rationale: Said Labour would replace the House of Lords with a democratically elected senate of the nations and regions, keeping a second chamber.

race-based-immigration-restrictions.rationale: Describes London's values as anti-racist and pledges to champion the rights and contribution of migrants irrespective of race.

torture-always-illegal.rationale: Told the Commons torture is illegal and internationally banned, that the House unequivocally condemns it and no government should have anything to do with it.

notes: Searched: 2024/2021 mayoral manifestos, City Hall press releases, Commons Hansard 2005-2016 (speeches and written answers), CNN/NPR transcripts 2016-2019, LabourList, JC and Arab News on Gaza. The record is mostly shadow-minister attack speeches, local-government manifestos and Trump-era interviews, so most statements on monarchy detail, secularism, gender theory, nationalism, foreign alliances, force and class theory have no recorded position and stay null. Not answered on purpose: rent-control (only a limited key-worker scheme), nuclear weapons, abortion, assisted dying, death penalty, reduce-immigration.
